title: Tokyo November CPI: a regional inflation update, not a mortgage repricing
summary: Tokyo's November mid-month preliminary CPI rose 2.8% year on year; excluding fresh food, it rose 2.9%. The 27 November release adds regional inflation evidence, without establishing a change in any lender's mortgage terms.

takeaways.text: Tokyo's November preliminary annual CPI increases were 2.8% overall, 2.9% excluding fresh food and 2.5% excluding fresh food and energy.
These are Tokyo ward-area statistics, not nationwide November results or a bank loan quotation.

sections.heading: What the official release says
sections.text: The Statistics Bureau published the November 2026 Tokyo ward-area mid-month preliminary CPI on 27 November 2026. On the 2025=100 base, the overall index was 103.8; the index excluding fresh food was 103.9; excluding fresh food and energy, it was 103.6. Their year-on-year increases were 2.8%, 2.9% and 2.5%, respectively. These measures have different coverage and should not be conflated.

sections.heading: What this means for mortgage comparisons
sections.text: This report's interpretation: regional inflation is context for monitoring financing conditions, but this statistical release establishes neither a BOJ policy decision nor a lender's repricing. It does not justify a deterministic rate forecast. Before comparing JPY mortgages, confirm the actual funding-month rate, variable versus initial-period or full-term fixed structure, eligibility, fees, insurance and contractual reset dates with the lender. No confirmed promotion is added by this update.

sections.heading: Dates and limits
sections.text: The reference month is November 2026 and the publication date is 27 November. This report was written on 27 November in Asia/Tokyo; source checks are separately recorded in UTC. The latest-results webpage can roll forward, so the release-specific official PDF is retained. No separate webpage modification timestamp was established. No loan offer validity period applies; the null effective dates do not assert continuing availability of a mortgage package.
